newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam says set for record trade gap in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says set for record trade gap in 1996.

text.p: Vietnam said on Saturday it notched up a near-record trade deficit of $3.489 billion in the first 10 months of 1996 and predicted the gap between imports and exports would widen even further.
A Trade Ministry official said the full-year deficit was expected to be $4.0 billion, the highest ever and up sharply from $2.3 billion in 1995.
Vietnam's reform-led economic boom and rapidly increasing income levels have brought an unprecedented boom in imports.
The government says a large proportion of its imports are capital goods which will ultimately generate production and exports.
But it has expressed concern about rapid growth in imports of consumer goods and some officials have suggested implementing a drive to substitute or even curb imports.
Trade Minister Le Van Triet this week told the National Assembly that the government had ordered ministries, industry sectors and local authorities to take steps to cut the trade deficit.

Voice of Vietnam quoted him as saying that imports should be managed more effectively and imports of supplies, materials, equipment and machinery which could be produced or supplied locally should be limited or halted.

The Trade Ministry said total trade volume in the first ten months of this year was $15.11 billion, a rise of 29.7 percent from the same period of 1995, with imports at $9.3 billion and exports at $5.81 billion.
The Government Statistics Office, which issues separate trade figures, recently reported a record trade gap of $3.54 billion for the period from January 1 to October 15.
